mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% and stable (change < 0.2% in 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% within a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 110), supply chain bottlenecks ease, boosting corporate margins and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO > 110, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures that prompt central banks to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher discount rates.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% for at least 3 months signals a tightening cycle, causing equity valuations to contract and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a labor market slowdown, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.2% and UNRATE rise > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines > 0.2% and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong manufacturing output (INDPRO > 110), supply chain efficiency improves, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO > 110, the S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
